security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU permits CLIC (aclic) interrupt-trap modifications to be active when mtvec.MODE = 0 (direct mode), causing interrupts and synchronous exceptions to share a single trap entry point while CLIC applies asymmetric save/restore behavior only to interrupts — spec explicitly forbids this combination
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: clic.*enabled|mclicbase.*enable|cliced.*enable without adjacent mtvec.mode != 0 guard; or CLIC trap-entry logic (GPR save/restore, stack switching) that does not branch on mtvec.MODE before applying interrupt-specific behavior
security_spec.summary: CLIC-enabled interrupt trap modifications (GPR save on interrupted stack) are incompatible with mtvec.MODE=0 shared entry points; QEMU must reject or fault this configuration to prevent asymmetric state corruption when exceptions and interrupts share a handler

findings.finding: In the current codebase, write_mtvec only enforces the standard MODE validity check (val & 3) < 2. There is no CLIC/mscratchcsw/mnxti interaction — CLIC is not implemented anywhere in QEMU's RISC-V emulation, so no CLIC+mtvec.MODE=0 guard is needed or missing. If CLIC is later added, a guard checking mtvec MODE != 0 when CLIC is enabled must be inserted here or in a CLIC write handler.

The S-mode trap-entry code checks (env->stvec & 3) == 1 for vectored mode — this is standard RISC-V behavior. No CLIC-specific save/restore (mscratchcsw, mnxti hardware update) exists because CLIC is unimplemented. The M-mode path (line 2488) similarly uses standard mcause/mepc save without any CLIC-specific logic.

The RISC-V Machine trap CSRs are defined from 0x340-0x35c, but CLIC CSRs (mnxti=0x345, mintstatus=0x346, mintthresh=0x347, mscratchcsw=0x348) are absent — no definitions exist. The address range is gapped (0x344 MIP then jumps to 0x350 MISELECT), confirming CLIC is unimplemented. No vulnerability possible without the CSRs.

Only CSR_MTVEC is registered in the CSR dispatch table. No CLIC CSRs (mnxti, mintstatus, mintthresh, mscratchcsw) are registered — any access to those CSR addresses would return an illegal-instruction exception by default, preventing any CLIC state manipulation.

The ISA extension table in cpu.c has no entry for Smclic, Ssclic, Zclic, or any CLIC extension. The cpu->cfg structure has no ext_smclic/ext_ssclic field. Without CLIC support, the CLIC+mtvec.MODE=0 vulnerability pattern cannot be triggered.
